newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen denies Thyssen-Krupp seeks stateaid.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen denies Thyssen-Krupp seeks stateaid.

text.p: Thyssen AG on Friday denied a newspaper report that Thyssen Krupp Stahl AG was seeking state subsidies from Bonn and Brussels to finance layoffs of 6,600 steel workers from the newly merged group.

Thyssen acknowledged that a personnel reduction of that scale was planned, and that talks had taken place in Bonn. Money to support such reductions comes not from the state but from a fund that European steel companies pay into for that purpose, Thyssen said.

"We have not applied in Bonn or Brussels for state subsidies to finance our social palns for the necessary reduction of 6,600 personnel, and will also not receive any such funds," said Thyssen spokeswoman Pascale Wiedenroth.
In a statement, the company said the steel fund was part of a decades-old policy of managing the downsizing of the European coal and steel industries.
Thyssen Krupp is the newly merged steel businesses of Thyssen AG and Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp.

Specific figures were not immediately available on how much money Thyssen Krupp was seeking, but previous similar actions have averaged about 35,000 marks ($20,300) per worker, which in this case would total 231 million marks, the daily Die Welt said.
The Berliner Zeitung reported that the European Commission was unlikely to take issue with the Thyssen Krupp merger.
